html:
In the Old Covenant of 1262 to 1264 the chieftains of Iceland agreed to become subjects of the king of Norway. It ended the Icelandic Commonwealth, which had governed itself without a king since 930.

In the 1200s a few great families fought a long civil war, the Age of the Sturlungs, and the Norwegian king played them off against each other. Snorri Sturluson was killed in 1241 in these struggles. Worn out, the Icelanders accepted the king in return for promises of peace, their own laws and regular shipping.

When Norway joined the Kalmar Union, Iceland passed with it under Danish rule, which lasted until the republic of 1944. The Althing lost most of its power. See Iceland.
